test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 15 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.

The director said, "The new actor will be arriving shortly."

options.text: The director said that the new actor would be arriving shortly.
The director said that the new actor will be arriving shortly.
The director said that the new actor would arrive shortly.
The director said that the new actor had been arriving shortly.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** The director said, "The new actor will be arriving shortly."
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Modal Verb Change (Backshifting):**
 
 
• When the reporting verb is in the past ("said"), modal verbs in the direct speech must shift to their past forms.
 
• The modal **"will"** changes to **"would."**
 
 
 
• **Tense Maintenance (Continuous Aspect):**
 
 
• The original sentence is in the Future Continuous ("will be arriving").
 
• In indirect speech, the continuous aspect **"be arriving"** is preserved after the shifted modal **"would."**
 
 
 
• **Conjunction:**
 
 
• The comma and quotation marks are removed and replaced by **"that"** to connect the reporting clause with the reported statement.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The director said that the new actor would be arriving shortly."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** Fails to shift the modal "will" to "would," which is necessary when the reporting verb is in the past.
 
• **Option 3:** Changes the aspect from continuous ("be arriving") to simple ("arrive"), which alters the original meaning of the speaker.
 
• **Option 4:** Uses the past perfect continuous ("had been arriving"), which incorrectly implies a past habitual action rather than a future planned arrival.
